title: Design database schema with constraints
description: Design PostgreSQL schema with proper constraints, indexes, and foreign keys to enforce business rules at DB level
design:
Tables:

1. coupons:
   - id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY
   - name VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL
   - amount INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (amount >= 0)
   - remaining_amount INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (remaining_amount >= 0)
   - created_at, updated_at TIMESTAMP

2. claims:
   - id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY  
   - user_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL
   - coupon_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL
   - claimed_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
   - UNIQUE(user_id, coupon_name) -- CRITICAL for preventing duplicate claims
   - FOREIGN KEY (coupon_name) REFERENCES coupons(name) ON DELETE CASCADE

Indexes:
- idx_coupons_name ON coupons(name)
- idx_claims_user_id ON claims(user_id)
- idx_claims_coupon_name ON claims(coupon_name)
acceptance_criteria:
- SQL schema file created with all tables
- UNIQUE constraint on (user_id, coupon_name) enforced
- Foreign key relationships defined
- Indexes created for performance
- CHECK constraints prevent negative amounts

title: Implement Coupon Repository
description: Implement repository pattern for Coupon CRUD operations with transaction support
design:
Interface:
type CouponRepository interface {
    Create(name string, amount int) error
    GetByName(name string) (*Coupon, error)
    GetByNameForUpdate(tx *sql.Tx, name string) (*Coupon, error)  // FOR UPDATE lock
    DecrementStock(tx *sql.Tx, name string) error
}

Key methods:
1. Create: INSERT INTO coupons
2. GetByName: SELECT * FROM coupons WHERE name = ?
3. GetByNameForUpdate: SELECT * FROM coupons WHERE name = ? FOR UPDATE (critical for locking)
4. DecrementStock: UPDATE coupons SET remaining_amount = remaining_amount - 1

Error handling:
- Return custom errors for not found, duplicate, etc.
acceptance_criteria:
- All CRUD methods implemented
- GetByNameForUpdate properly locks row
- Methods accept *sql.Tx for transaction support
- Unit tests for each method
- Error handling for edge cases

title: Implement Claim Repository
description: Implement repository for Claim operations with UNIQUE constraint violation handling
design:
Interface:
type ClaimRepository interface {
    Insert(tx *sql.Tx, userID, couponName string) error
    GetByCouponName(couponName string) ([]Claim, error)
}

Key methods:
1. Insert: INSERT INTO claims (user_id, coupon_name) VALUES (?, ?)
   - Must detect UNIQUE constraint violations (pq error code 23505)
   - Return custom ErrAlreadyClaimed error

2. GetByCouponName: SELECT * FROM claims WHERE coupon_name = ?
   - Returns array of all claims for a coupon

Error handling:
- Check for *pq.Error type
- Map error code 23505 to ErrAlreadyClaimed
- Return meaningful errors
acceptance_criteria:
- Insert method detects UNIQUE constraint violations
- Returns ErrAlreadyClaimed for duplicate claims
- GetByCouponName returns all claims correctly
- Methods accept *sql.Tx for transactions
- Unit tests verify constraint handling

title: Implement Coupon Service with atomic transactions
description: Implement service layer with atomic claim transaction logic - THE CRITICAL COMPONENT
design:
Interface:
type CouponService interface {
    CreateCoupon(name string, amount int) error
    ClaimCoupon(userID, couponName string) error
    GetCouponDetails(name string) (*CouponDetails, error)
}

CRITICAL: ClaimCoupon transaction flow:
1. BEGIN TRANSACTION
2. Lock coupon: repo.GetByNameForUpdate(tx, couponName)
3. Check stock: if coupon.RemainingAmount <= 0 return ErrNoStock
4. Insert claim: repo.InsertClaim(tx, userID, couponName)
   - If UNIQUE violation -> ROLLBACK, return ErrAlreadyClaimed (409)
5. Decrement stock: repo.DecrementStock(tx, couponName)
6. COMMIT TRANSACTION

Error types:
- ErrAlreadyClaimed -> HTTP 409
- ErrNoStock -> HTTP 400
- ErrCouponNotFound -> HTTP 404

The SELECT FOR UPDATE is what prevents race conditions!
acceptance_criteria:
- ClaimCoupon uses single atomic transaction
- SELECT FOR UPDATE locks coupon row
- Constraint violations detected and mapped
- All operations rollback on error
- Transaction commits only if all steps succeed
- Custom error types for each failure case

title: Write Flash Sale concurrency test (50 requests, 5 stock)
description: CRITICAL TEST: Verify exactly 5 claims succeed when 50 concurrent users attack 5-item stock coupon
design:
Test scenario:
1. Setup: Create coupon with amount=5
2. Execute: Spawn 50 goroutines, each making claim request with different user_id
3. Collect: Gather all 50 HTTP response codes
4. Assert:
   - Exactly 5 responses with 200/201 (success)
   - Exactly 45 responses with 400 (no stock)
   - GET coupon shows remaining_amount=0
   - GET coupon shows claimed_by array has exactly 5 users
   - Database claims table has exactly 5 records

Implementation:
- Use sync.WaitGroup to coordinate goroutines
- Use buffered channel to collect results
- Use http.Client to make real HTTP requests
- Run against dockerized API (not mocked)

This test MUST pass for submission!
acceptance_criteria:
- Test spawns 50 concurrent goroutines
- Exactly 5 claims succeed (200/201)
- Exactly 45 claims fail (400 no stock)
- remaining_amount = 0 after test
- No race conditions detected
- Test is deterministic and repeatable

title: Write Double Dip concurrency test (10 requests, same user)
description: CRITICAL TEST: Verify exactly 1 claim succeeds when same user makes 10 concurrent requests
design:
Test scenario:
1. Setup: Create coupon with amount=100
2. Execute: Spawn 10 goroutines, ALL using SAME user_id
3. Collect: Gather all 10 HTTP response codes
4. Assert:
   - Exactly 1 response with 200/201 (success)
   - Exactly 9 responses with 409 (already claimed)
   - GET coupon shows remaining_amount=99
   - GET coupon shows claimed_by array has exactly 1 user
   - Database claims table has exactly 1 record for this user

Implementation:
- Use sync.WaitGroup to coordinate goroutines
- Use buffered channel to collect results
- Use SAME user_id for all requests
- Run against dockerized API

This test validates UNIQUE constraint enforcement!
acceptance_criteria:
- Test spawns 10 concurrent goroutines
- All goroutines use same user_id
- Exactly 1 claim succeeds (200/201)
- Exactly 9 claims fail (409 already claimed)
- remaining_amount = 99 after test
- No duplicate claims in database
- Test is deterministic and repeatable
